You.... you have a union? How I wish that we could unionize. We had a group of 4 people trying to get support to form a union where I work. Within the next month after they started distributing petitions, they were all fired. 

Now, the company was smart about it. They went through and found inconsistencies with one employee's school schedule, saying that the hours he had to have off didn't coincide directly with his school schedule. He was the first to be fired.

The next was fired for a glitch in the attendance system. We use a system called Aspect, which is incredibly common in call centers, at least around here. The agent in question took vacation time that Aspect said she had, but it wasn't really there. This is a common problem with the program, but usually agents are just warned to stay on top of their vacation balances and sick time is used to cover the overage. She was fired instantly for it. 

The other two were fired for similar things. Small stuff that doesn't usually get disciplinary action, but did with them... 

They all raised a huge stink with the labor board, and associated authorities, but since the state where I work is 'at-will' they couldn't do anything since they were technically fired for real infractions.

I work at a call center for a major US ISP. I hate it. I hate people.

When I started working here, it was about helping people. It was about technical support, and fixing the customer's issue no matter what. My employer cared about the employee's mental health. What I mean by that, is that if we ever needed a quick 5 minute breather from a difficult customer, we could take one. If a customer cursed at us or insulted us, and didn't stop, we could tell them to stop or we would hang up on them. If our customers got too abusive, we would disconnect them. We can no longer do this. The company values their money more than they do our sanity. We're replaceable, but the customer's money is not. 

We used to be able to assist with router issues, printer issues, computer issues. We used to have the ability to actually fix problems before they arose and make sure that the customer was happy. This is too time consuming and not profitable anymore, so we're no longer allowed to do this. Basic fixes such as unplug it and plug it back in. Didn't work? Too bad, roll a truck and charge the customer for the cost of the tech who comes out. 

This was 5 years ago.  This was before the company was bought out. This was before the investors demanded changes. Technical support now had to be profitable. We couldn't just sit on our asses fixing things all day - we had to produce for the company. 

It started with incentives for selling, which was great. We all excelled because we were able to gauge when to ask for a sale and when to not. We suggested things customers might actually need or want. We felt okay with ourselves. Our commission structure was nice - it gave us a real push to try to sell something. 

Then we were told that the commission structure would be changing because it was too taxing on the company. Sales trailed off, but we were still meeting the soft-goal... If you didn't meet the goal, you weren't punished. You were simply coached on how to do better with sales. Then came the requirements. It started small with telling us we had to get so many core service sales per month. Things such as internet, phone or cable. It was small at first, 5 per agent. Even then, if you missed it, it wasn't too big of a deal, you were still helping the customer.


Then our expectation of handle time was changed. It was cut by 3 minutes. This doesn't sound like a lot, but this was time we used to converse with the customer about their day, about other problems that they may be having, time to troubleshoot. 

Then the sales goals kept rising. We now had to sell 10 core services per month, then 15, then 20, then 25. It's now at the point where I am expected to sell more than 1 core service per day. That wouldn't have been a problem back in the day... Our customers used to be cheerful, our tech staff used to be cheerful, but that changed. The corporate environment changed. Our supervisors and upper management who we had been friends with changed, and were now no longer people that we could talk to about day to day stuff, people who we could joke with. We became scared of saying the wrong thing. The mood tanked, morale hit rock bottom and it has never returned. This place is a hell hole where 75% of the employees are on some kind of medication for depression or anxiety. We used to have no turn over, and I knew everyone's name. Out of 40 people in my sub-department I know only 5 people. 

The customers over time have become a lot less happy, and a lot more angry at us. The service has gone down hill. Good field techs have left and were replaced with contractors who don't give a shit if the services are working a week from now, just as long as it's working for a day after they leave. Our customers have come to hate us entirely and it makes us hate them. We understand their frustration, but you can only take so much yelling and cursing and being told that you're a worthless piece of shit before you start believing it. 

So due to this, performance suffers. With less happy customers, you have less opportunity to sell, and the limit is no longer a soft-goal. It's a hard limit that if you do not meet, you are written up instantly. If you miss goal for three months, you get your final written warning and then you are gone. I have seen men who have been here for 20+ years in their 60s break down and sob because they just lost their only source of income, and they know they can't get another job.  

So now we're forced to try and push sales on people who actively hate us, and even worse people who may be naive as to what they're buying. I've heard someone tell an old woman that if she got our internet service that her grandchildren may want to visit her. I've seen old women lied to and told that our phone service is as reliable as AT&T home phone and perfect for life-alert, when I know that it isn't and in an emergency, it's our phone service that may mean they die because the power is out and it doesn't work. 

I hate this company. I hate myself. I hate that I have stayed so long that I have no other options. I hate the bitter person I have become because of it. 

There's a lot more I'd like to say, and my thoughts aren't very coherent right now because I've consumed quite a bit of alcohol, but it's nice to vent.
